rationale: Blind, edge-case, and acceptance lenses all ran with real (non-empty) output against the full 9-commit diff. Two of the blind lens's claims (missing auth on admin routes; unguarded update_conversation_history_by_index) were verified false positives caused by diff-only isolation (router-level admin_access_only dependency and the delegated assert_mutable() guard were confirmed present by direct source inspection). Five real findings survive triage: a migration correctness bug that defeats the feature's own scheduler-discovery use case (CR-001), two unmodified read paths that silently misreport isFinished (CR-002), a spec-vs-implementation mismatch on response casing that needs a decision (CR-003), dead filter plumbing (CR-004), and a data-durability race in the shared update() path that is more severe than the spec's already-accepted 'minor race' language (CR-005, decision_needed). 6 findings dismissed (2 false positives, 3 deliberate/precedent-matching design choices already reasoned in plan.md, 1 explicitly-accepted-in-spec race). 5 findings deferred as real-but-out-of-approved-scope (pre-persistence agent-dispatch cost check, OFFSET pagination skip risk, bulk sequential round trips, history-deletion endpoints left unguarded consistent with spec's deletion carve-out, and test_ability_conversation.py left untouched since it reuses already-tested Ability primitives). Commit-message capitalization deviates from repo convention (cosmetic, noted in standards_review, not blocking).

findings.title: Migration leaves pre-existing rows with is_finished=NULL, breaking scheduler discovery
findings.problem: op.add_column("conversations", sa.Column("is_finished", sa.Boolean(), nullable=True, default=False)) uses only a Python-side ORM default, not server_default, and there is no backfill UPDATE. Every conversation that existed before this migration runs keeps is_finished=NULL.
findings.impact: SQL equality (is_finished = false) treats NULL as unknown, not true. Both the new partial index predicate and every is_finished=False filter added in this diff (get_all_conversations_admin, _build_filter_sql) silently exclude all pre-migration conversations. GET /admin/conversations?isFinished=false — the scheduler's headline query per AC6/AC9 — will miss the entire pre-migration dataset, defeating the feature's core purpose.
findings.recommendation: Add server_default=sa.false() to the column definition, or run an explicit UPDATE conversations SET is_finished = false WHERE is_finished IS NULL after adding the column, in the same migration's upgrade().

findings.title: Two paginated read paths never populate is_finished/finished_at
findings.problem: ConversationService.get_user_conversations_paginated (backing GET /conversations?page=&per_page=) and get_conversation_history_slice (backing the paginated branch of GET /conversations/{id}) were not updated to select or populate is_finished/finished_at; both leave the fields at their ConversationListItem/ConversationResponse defaults.
findings.impact: Any client using pagination on the list or get-by-id endpoints always sees isFinished=false regardless of actual state, violating AC5's 'every read/list path surfaces state' requirement for two commonly-used paginated entry points.
findings.recommendation: Add is_finished/finished_at to the SQL SELECT and the ConversationListItem/response construction in both methods, mirroring the pattern already applied to get_user_conversations and search_by_name_and_user.

findings.title: ConversationListItem/ConversationResponse emit snake_case, not the camelCase the spec claims
findings.problem: spec.md states the new fields are 'serialized as isFinished/finishedAt via the existing ConfiguredModel camelCase alias convention,' but ConversationListItem and ConversationResponse are plain BaseModel subclasses with no alias generator (all their existing sibling fields are already snake_case). Only the new ConversationFinishResult/ConversationFinishBulkRequest/ConversationFinishBulkResponse DTOs use ConfiguredModel.
findings.impact: The finish endpoints return isFinished/finishedAt/alreadyFinished (camelCase) while the get/list/search endpoints return is_finished/finished_at (snake_case) for the conceptually identical field — an inconsistent wire contract for any FE consumer building against both endpoint families.
findings.recommendation: Needs a decision, not a unilateral fix: migrating ConversationListItem/ConversationResponse to ConfiguredModel would change the wire format of every existing field on those two DTOs (a breaking change for current consumers). Alternatives: accept and document the inconsistency, or add per-field aliases scoped to only the two new fields. Surface to the user/spec owner rather than picking one silently.

findings.title: is_finished filter column is allowed but never wired to a route
findings.problem: _build_filter_sql's allowed_filter_columns gained "is_finished", but GET /conversations has no isFinished query parameter, and both call sites of Conversation.get_user_conversations (routers/conversation.py, routers/ide.py) call it without a filters dict.
findings.impact: AC6's claim that is_finished 'can be used as the user list-endpoint query filter (isFinished=true|false)' is unfulfilled — a user-facing client cannot actually filter their own conversation list by finished state.
findings.recommendation: Add an isFinished query parameter to the GET /conversations route and thread it into the filters dict passed to get_user_conversations, or remove the allowed_filter_columns entry if this filter was intentionally deferred to a follow-on.

findings.title: Conversation.update()'s session.merge() can silently un-finish a conversation under concurrent write
findings.problem: BaseModelWithSQLSupport.update() calls session.merge(self), which writes the full in-memory attribute state of the Python object, not a diff against the current DB row. If a content-mutation request loads a Conversation before a concurrent finish request commits, and then calls .update() after the finish committed, the mutation request's stale in-memory is_finished=False is merged back over the DB, reverting the just-finished conversation to unfinished.
findings.impact: This is more severe than the spec's accepted 'minor race conditions between a concurrent append and finish' (which describes ordering of an append landing near a finish, not the finish's own persisted state being silently erased by an unrelated write). A conversation an admin/scheduler just finished can end up mutable again with no error or log signal.
findings.recommendation: Needs a decision given the spec already accepts some raced behavior here: options include a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE is_finished = false at persist time, re-checking assert_mutable() immediately before the merge/commit, or explicitly confirming with the user that this specific failure mode (finish silently reverted) is also within the accepted risk — it reads as a materially different and worse outcome than what was described as accepted.
